transcript.text: Good afternoon, everyone. I'd like to begin our routine check-in for the restored silent film "The Last Harbor" before we lock the final presentation package. I'll need to hear from each of you on the archive, music, and technical aspects of the current draft — which proposes digital projection, a live string trio, and the standard 16:9 screen mask. Let's start with whoever is responsible for the archive side of things.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Good afternoon, Mara. I'm glad we're doing this check-in before the package is locked, because I have an important update on the archive side. I received an archive-license amendment yesterday that directly affects our current draft presentation package. I need to share the specifics of that amendment with everyone before we proceed.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Good afternoon, Mara. While Julian covers the archive update, I want to flag that I have a significant technical finding from this morning's screening room test that also affects the current draft package. I'll share the details as soon as we're ready for the technical check-in.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thank you both for flagging these updates. Julian, please go ahead and share the specifics of that archive-license amendment now. Nia, we'll come to your technical finding right after. I want to hear everything before I make any decisions on the final package.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I reviewed an archive-license amendment received yesterday confirming that this festival screening must use the Northlight Archive's 35mm print, retain the film's 1.33:1 image framing without cropping, and display the exact credit 'Restored by Northlight Archive'. I have not yet entered the amendment into the festival rights tracker. This means our current draft proposing digital projection and the standard 16:9 screen mask is not compliant with the amended license terms.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: This morning I tested the screening room with the live-score setup and confirmed that the room's pit and monitoring arrangement supports only a solo piano, not the proposed string trio. The commissioned score cleared for this performance is 'Tide Marks,' and I have not yet updated the technical run sheet. This means the current draft's live string trio proposal is not technically feasible in our screening room as it stands.
transcript.speaker: A3

commitments.detail: Enter the archive-license amendment into the festival rights tracker.
Update the technical run sheet to reflect solo piano accompaniment and the screening room pit/monitoring arrangement.

Revise the draft presentation package to replace digital projection with 35mm print, replace 16:9 screen mask with 1.33:1 framing, and replace string trio with solo piano performing 'Tide Marks,' including the 'Restored by Northlight Archive' credit.
